Quantum Papers Aggregator A fully automated, serverless research tool that collects and displays the latest academic papers in quantum computing and spin qubits from arXiv — refreshed every morning with zero manual effort.
Live site: 0xr101.github.io/Papers_Aggregator
Overview Keeping up with the pace of quantum computing research is hard. New papers appear on arXiv every day across multiple categories, and manually checking them is time-consuming. This project solves that by automating the entire pipeline — from fetching raw data to displaying it in a clean, searchable interface — with no server, no database, and no ongoing cost.

I am a PhD researcher in Theoretical Physics at King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals (KFUPM), specializing in Condensed Matter Physics and quantum information processing. My doctoral research is currently conducted at the Interdisciplinary Research Center for Advanced Quantum Computing, under the supervision of Professor Daniel Loss.
My academic journey is driven by a deep interest in the fundamental mechanics of quantum systems and the physical realization of quantum computation. Prior to my doctoral studies, I completed my undergraduate degree with highest honors (3.96/4.00 CGPA), developing a rigorous foundation in physics alongside advanced computational and engineering methodologies. During my senior year, I also served as the President of the Physics Club, fostering academic engagement within the student body.
title: About Me

summary:
In this post, we will briefly explore the fundamental mechanisms governing spin qubits confined in semiconductor quantum dots.
The time evolution of the electron spin state in the presence of an external magnetic field is determined by the Zeeman Hamiltonian. We can express this fundamental relationship as:
$$\hat{H} = \frac{1}{2} g \mu_B \vec{B} \cdot \vec{\sigma}$$Where:
$g$ is the Landé g-factor. $\mu_B$ is the Bohr magneton. $\vec{B}$ is the applied magnetic field vector. $\vec{\sigma}$ represents the Pauli spin matrices. Further experimental data and computational models using QuTiP will be discussed in upcoming publications.
title: Dynamics of Spin Qubits in Semiconductor Quantum Dots

summary:
Landauer’s principle establishes a fundamental lower bound on the energy consumption of irreversible computation. By employing reversible computing architectures, we theoretically circumvent this thermodynamic limit.
This research focuses on the optimization of quantum logic gates to minimize energy dissipation.
Current Benchmarks Recent simulations indicate a significant reduction in gate error rates when applying optimized pulse sequences. The transition from classical logical irreversibility to quantum reversibility requires a paradigm shift in how we approach circuit design.
title: Energy Efficiency in Reversible Quantum Circuits
